1.

On our request, Dr. Saraf, learned Advocate General has appeared, so as to appraise the Court on a vital issue namely in regard to the constitution of the "Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority", as per the provision of Section 51 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the 2013 Act") to be made functional for different parts of the State of Maharashtra to exercise jurisdiction to adjudicate references as contemplated by Section 64 of the 2013 Act.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner has raised a contention that as on date only one authority is constituted which functions from Nagpur which,
according
to the petitioners, is overburdened with Section 64 references being filed from all over the State.
2. Dr. Saraf on instructions however submits that there is one more authority established at Aurangabad.
It is his submission that the State Government is in the process of taking a decision in regard to constitution of more authorities.

Dr. Saraf states that in the past a meeting was held with the Hon'ble the Acting Chief Justice which was in pursuance of observations made by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court raising similar concerns.

3. We may observe that the functions of the Authority to be constituted under Section 51 are extremely important in the administration and implementation of the 2013 Act, namely to adjudicate land acquisition 12 June, 2024 Kiran Kawre 901-02-03-WPL-1220-2024.DOC references.
Such jurisdiction is akin to the jurisdiction exercised by the Civil Court under Section 18 and Section 30 under the regime of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

4. Learned Counsel for the petitioners has brought to our notice that in smaller States, illustratively in the State of Kerala, there are 14 authorities which are constituted to adjudicate the references filed under Section 64.
5.

Hence there is much substance in the petitioners' concern that only one or two Authorities being constituted for large State like Maharashtra would not suffice, and this would prejudice litigants in effective adjudication of their references filed under Section 64 of the 2013 Act, which a substantive legal remedy available to the parties.
This would directly affect the citizens rights of access to justice.

6. We are quite confident that the State Government with all the consciousness at its command,
would not let the litigants in the State of Maharashtra, being deprived of the right to speedy and Sharifa Ismail Loladiya vs The Principal Secretary Revenue And ... on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130681510/
2 effective adjudication of references under Section 64 of the 2013 Act, merely for the reason that sufficient number of Authorities to cater to different territorial jurisdictions are not appointed.

We, accordingly, permit the State Government to place on record an affidavit of a responsible officer on the steps it would intend to take to appoint more numbers of authorities for different territorial jurisdictions as Section 51 of the 2013 Act would mandate.
8. We adjourn the proceeding to 27 June 2024.
9. List these petitions alongwith Writ Petition (L) No.1305 of 2024.
